Problems found; follow the advice item by item
Could not read the run status
Start the network, wait a few seconds, then tap Run again.
Create and select a network on the Networks page, then return here.
No server address configured; only incoming connections are possible
Add the other side\'s tcp://host:11010 in Servers. For passive access, give them the listener address and allow the port.
No server address; cannot join the network
Enter at least one server address, e.g. tcp://1.2.3.4:11010. Use the EasyTier listener port on the server.
Use protocol://host:port, e.g. tcp://1.2.3.4:11010. Supports tcp/udp/ws/wss/wg/quic/ring.
Remove blank server addresses to avoid confusing the runtime configuration.
Enter a network name that exactly matches the other side (case-sensitive).
Set a network secret so others cannot join; it must also exactly match.
Network name and secret are set
DHCP is on while a static IPv4 %1$s is set
DHCP overrides the static IPv4. Turn off DHCP to keep a fixed IP, or clear the static IPv4 to use automatic assignment.
DHCP is off and no static IPv4 is set
Turn on DHCP or enter a static IP (e.g. 10.144.144.10/24), otherwise no virtual IP is assigned.
P2P only and Disable P2P are both on and conflict
Both on at once allows neither direct nor relayed connections. Keep P2P only for direct; turn off Disable P2P for relayed.
Server reachability cannot be confirmed directly
Confirm EasyTier is running and listening on that port on the server; allow it in the cloud security group, firewall, and router port forwarding. If the domain fails, check DNS or use the IP.
No UDP reply does not mean the service is down. Prefer a tcp:// address when connections fail so TCP probing can confirm the port.
ring addresses are resolved by the relay service and cannot be probed directly
UDP probing only shows a packet was sent; it cannot confirm the port is open
Connection timed out (3 s); the server is unreachable or dropped by the firewall
Connection refused; the port is closed or blocked by the firewall
Host unreachable; wrong address or route
A UDP probe was sent but no reply arrived; no UDP reply can still be normal
Go back to Home, tap Connect, wait until connected, then diagnose again.
If this lasts long, check the server address, port, and firewall, and read the event log below.
First confirm the server is reachable. For authentication or decryption errors, check the network name and secret. Read the latest error in the event log.
Running, but no other peers found yet
Confirm the network name and secret exactly match. Confirm the server is reachable and hosts peers on the same network. If the network is new, wait for peers to join.
All %1$d peers are relayed; none are direct
Disable P2P is on, so all traffic must be relayed; turn it off for direct connections.
P2P only is on but traffic is still relayed, so a direct link was not established.
Symmetric NAT detected; UDP hole punching usually fails. Enable the KCP or QUIC proxy in the editor for steadier traffic.
Enable the KCP or QUIC proxy in the editor to improve relay quality. Also check whether Disable P2P was turned on by mistake.
Latency and packet loss are normal
High latency: use a closer server or relay, enable KCP/QUIC proxying, and check the Wi-Fi or mobile signal.
High loss: disable battery limits, avoid weak Wi-Fi, and confirm the server bandwidth is not saturated.
The device has a usable network
The device has no usable network
Turn on Wi-Fi or mobile data and wait until the system reports a usable network before diagnosing or connecting.
Allow it in the system dialog when you tap Connect on Home. If you denied it, allow Timiao in System settings > Network > VPN.
The system is limiting Timiao\'s background activity
Set System settings > Battery > Unrestricted so Timiao stays in the background; otherwise the VPN may disconnect when the screen locks.
Allow notifications; otherwise the foreground service status is hidden and some systems clean up background work more aggressively.
No kernel event log was collected
Connect and run the network for a few seconds, then tap Run again.
No abnormal events were recorded recently
No errors among the latest %1$d events
The server port is closed: confirm EasyTier is running and allow the port in the firewall and cloud security group.
Connection timed out: check the server address, port forwarding, and firewall rules.
DNS resolution failed: check the domain spelling and DNS settings, or use an IP address.
Network unreachable: check the phone network, proxy settings, and any conflicting VPN.
Handshake or authentication failed: check the network name and secret, and confirm both sides use compatible versions.
Fix the fatal event above (virtual NIC or IP conflict), then reconnect.
Use the event details above to check the server status, network name, and secret.
